name: tarroo-ushtey

attributes.attribute: water bull of the Isle of Man
blighted crops rather than eating people

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The tarroo-ushtey was the water bull of the Isle of Man. It was far less fierce than most water beasts. Other monsters of the deep ate people and cattle. The tarroo-ushtey only ruined the farmers' crops. The farmer could guard against it with a wand of rowan. The rod from the rowan tree turned it away.

okr.objective: Record the tarroo-ushtey as the mild water bull of the Isle of Man.
key_results: Identifies the tarroo-ushtey as a Manx water bull
States it blighted crops rather than devoured people
Notes a rowan wand could stop it
